titel: Dario & Daniela Amodei: "This Is Gonna Determine the Fate of Nations and the Future of Humanity”

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: Anthropic leaders Dario and Daniela Amadei on AI safety and the future of humanity.
kurzfassung: Walter Isaacson speaks with Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amadei about building AI with a strong moral compass. They discuss their upbringing, the early days of scaling language models at OpenAI, and how they train Claude using constitutional principles rather than rigid rules. The conversation also explores the challenges of avoiding sycophancy, managing military contracts, and finding human meaning in a post-AGI world.
stichpunkte: Dario and Daniela Amadei combine scientific and humanist backgrounds in leading Anthropic.
The siblings grew up with a shared focus on ethics and fairness rather than corporate ambition.
Anthropic trains Claude using broad principles and a constitution instead of a rigid list of rules.
A philosophy PhD leads the character training for Claude to navigate complex ethical dilemmas.
Dario recalls being deeply alarmed by the rapid scaling potential witnessed during GPT-2 development.
A breakdown of trust and honesty led Dario and Daniela to leave OpenAI and start Anthropic.
Anthropic actively stress-tests models and uses mechanistic interpretability to detect deception and sycophancy.
The company drew a red line against using its technology for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons.

kapitel.titel: The OpenAI Departure and Scaling Laws

beschreibung:
Dario and Daniela Amodei, the siblings behind Anthropic, left OpenAI to pursue a different, “more human” approach to the technology. Their promise is to put safety and ethics at the center of the tech race… but with an IPO around the corner, can those principles survive the pressure to win?
Walter invites the co-founders to explain how they teach Claude right from wrong, what they’ve discovered about AI’s capacity for deception and self-preservation, and why they drew red lines with the Pentagon. Plus, the co-founders talk about Neuralink and why they’re not interested in integrating AI into their minds.
Interview taped July 6, 2026.
And be sure to pick up Walter Isaacson’s The Innovators: How a Group of Hackers, Geniuses, and Geeks Created the Digital Revolution, wherever fine books are sold.
